controls.title: Evidence records are structurally linked
controls.scope: LOG.md, WHY.md, PARKED.md, CHANGELOG.md, and README.md in this repository
controls.assertion: Run the documentation-record structural tests.
controls.expected: All record IDs are unique, required fields exist, and every cross-reference resolves.
controls.evidence: pytest output and the release conformance JSON report
controls.blind_spots: Does not determine whether narrative content is substantively true.

controls.title: Known prohibited claim forms remain absent
controls.scope: Current product README, SECURITY, Enterprise Python, Ultra JavaScript, and current assurance profiles
controls.assertion: Run the bounded claim-language regression test.
controls.expected: No known banned phrase or prospective-partner documentation directory is present.
controls.evidence: pytest output and the release conformance JSON report
controls.blind_spots: Natural-language claim detection is partial and does not understand every possible paraphrase.

controls.title: Unknown classifications fail closed
controls.scope: Classification labels, policy/profile construction, and LedgerObserver ingress
controls.assertion: Run label, policy, classified-mode, observer, and red-team suites.
controls.expected: All named suites pass, including malformed-classification denial tests.
controls.evidence: pytest output and the release conformance JSON report
controls.blind_spots: Does not intercept markings parsed by code outside these modules.

controls.title: Governed MCP actuation composes mandatory gates
controls.scope: GovernedRuntime and Enterprise MCP dispatcher actuation paths
controls.assertion: Run governed-runtime and MCP dispatcher tests.
controls.expected: Policy trust root, live target, approval context, control plane, persistent ledger, transport enqueue, and new UIA readback gates pass or fail closed.
controls.evidence: pytest output and the release conformance JSON report
controls.blind_spots: Direct SDK calls and other repositories are not globally intercepted; deterministic tests do not establish a live Windows target.

controls.title: Durable operator transitions require signed evidence before authority
controls.scope: DurableOperatorQueue, GovernedRuntime approval composition, and MCP mutation through the governed dispatcher
controls.assertion: Run ledger, approval-audit, governed-runtime, policy, and MCP dispatcher tests.
controls.expected: Ledger state advances only after durable append; approval transitions remain non-authorizing during audit failure; finalization revalidates under a write transaction; decision proof envelopes are bounded and nonce-bound; durable nonce tombstones survive approval purge for the configured horizon; consume APIs use only the validated constructor clock; approval and outbox schemas plus foreign keys are independently checked; exact disk-snapshot receipt verification rejects cache aliasing; and mutation requires one unique pending-to-approved-to-consumed lineage with every signed receipt verified.
controls.evidence: pytest output, hosted CI, and the release conformance JSON report
controls.blind_spots: The repository does not select or assess a deployment's CAC/PKI/operator credential verifier or trusted clock; nonce tombstones provide bounded rather than indefinite replay history; the unkeyed context digest is not confidentiality protection; direct SDK and non-governed queue use are outside scope; exact-once reconciliation assumes one ledger writer and does not coordinate multiple processes; the typed in-memory approval index has first-use scan and retained-memory cost.

controls.title: Terminal target identity uses protected image paths
controls.scope: Current target_guard mappings for Windows Terminal and classic Windows console classes
controls.assertion: Run the target-guard load and class-spoof test.
controls.expected: Live HWND enumeration completes deterministically, user-writable lookalike image paths are refused, and protected Windows/package paths are accepted.
controls.evidence: Target-guard load-test output and the release conformance JSON report
controls.blind_spots: Does not validate Authenticode signers or protect a compromised trusted binary, administrator, or kernel; unmapped terminal classes fail closed.

controls.title: Live governed terminal delivery and execution effect
controls.scope: One inspected live Windows terminal HWND, one signed policy/identity, one bounded command, and its signed action ledger
controls.assertion: Run tools.irs_runtime_conformance with --execute and an --expect-output token that is absent from --text, then independently read the target.
controls.expected: Target binding and policy pass; UIA confirms a new payload occurrence; the separate output token newly appears; the signed ledger verifies.
controls.evidence: Conformance JSON, independent UIA readback, screenshot hash if retained, exact target metadata, and ledger verification result
controls.blind_spots: A result applies only to the tested terminal version, shell, policy, identity, action, session, and machine. It is not external-workflow, WORM, government-authorization, or scale evidence.

controls.title: Ultra lifecycle proofs reject tamper and replay
controls.scope: Ultra agent-auth verifier and production-store unit/integration tests available in the current environment
controls.assertion: Run the Ultra Node test suite.
controls.expected: Authentication tests pass; PostgreSQL tests pass when DATABASE_URL is supplied and otherwise report an explicit skip.
controls.evidence: Node test output and the release conformance JSON report
controls.blind_spots: A skipped PostgreSQL suite is not production durability evidence.

controls.title: BPC abuse and shadow responses fail closed
controls.scope: Ultra BPC verification composition, source-IP and pair rate-limit wiring, and shadow/ghost authorization conversion
controls.assertion: Run the Ultra Node unit suite and the live Python adversarial suite when a production sidecar is available.
controls.expected: Unit tests reject shadow and ghost responses; live tests show a quarantined source-IP/pair tuple cannot authorize with a fresh valid credential.
controls.evidence: Node/Python test output and the release or live conformance report
controls.blind_spots: Repository tests do not select production thresholds, establish deployment capacity, or prevent abuse arriving through another unregistered service path.

controls.title: Ultra recovery and TSK rotation are bound and retry-safe
controls.scope: Recovery-token claim binding, one-generation verification overlap, TSK prepare/commit/resume, and identity-binding compare-and-swap
controls.assertion: Run Ultra Node tests and the Python lifecycle suite; perform the production overlap/restart/retirement ceremony for deployment evidence.
controls.expected: Token claim tampering fails, one previous verification key is bounded, TSK retries preserve one committed binding, and the old client is revoked.
controls.evidence: Node/Python test output, rotation conformance output, and production restart evidence
controls.blind_spots: Unit success does not establish secret-manager custody, service-account ACLs, operator separation, or an executed deployment ceremony.

controls.title: Signed local ledger segments retain one verified sequence
controls.scope: AgentLedger local append, segment sealing, restart continuation, archive ordering, and corruption refusal
controls.assertion: Run the AgentLedger test suite.
controls.expected: Entry/byte threshold rotation, cross-segment verification, restart continuation, missing-middle detection, and corrupt-startup refusal all pass.
controls.evidence: pytest output and the release conformance report
controls.blind_spots: Local segmentation cannot detect removal of the complete ledger or final tail without a separately trusted checkpoint and is not centralized retention evidence.

controls.title: Hardened provenance uses a fail-closed local service contract
controls.scope: Dedicated provenance service configuration, signed IPC, endpoint discovery, PID and key binding, durable request recovery, filesystem ACL checks, and hardened-profile client composition
controls.assertion: Run the provenance service, IPC, client, Windows pipe, deployment-contract, and hardened runtime composition suites.
controls.expected: Named unit and local Windows tests pass for service identity, explicit sessions, replay/freshness/signature denial, PID/key binding, low-integrity denial, ACL drift refusal, recovery, and no hardened-profile in-process fallback.
controls.evidence: pytest output, release conformance report, and the separately scoped installed-service acceptance artifact
controls.blind_spots: Repository tests do not install through SCM under distinct operating-system tokens, exercise forced service restart, configure off-host retention, prove remote-host rejection, or create an authorization.

controls.title: Installed provenance service boundary is exercised under distinct Windows tokens
controls.scope: One reviewed wheel, one Windows host, SCM, a restricted virtual service account, disposable non-admin client tokens, the local named-pipe boundary, signed ledgers, and uninstall cleanup
controls.assertion: From elevated PowerShell, run deploy/provenance_service_acceptance.ps1 against the exact reviewed wheel and retain a redacted report.
controls.expected: Install, enrollment, valid commit, adversarial denials, low-integrity denial, endpoint rotation, DACL tamper refusal, forced restart recovery, offline chain/index verification, uninstall, and cleanup all pass.
controls.evidence: docs/operations/2026-07-16-provenance-service-acceptance.json plus the owner-retained raw report and transcript hashes
controls.blind_spots: The recorded run used a local memory witness, not off-host WORM storage. Remote-host pipe rejection requires a second Windows host. One host/build/configuration does not establish other deployments or an authorization.

controls.title: IRS-neutral evidence validates inventory, review, and record kind
controls.scope: Local IRS use-case/model/data/action evidence schema and its signed AgentLedger recorder
controls.assertion: Run the IRS evidence contract tests.
controls.expected: Deployed inventory references model/data records, executed high-impact actions require completed review, and prompt/test/incident kinds derive their stated retention labels.
controls.evidence: pytest output, signed test ledger verification, and the release conformance report
controls.blind_spots: A retention label does not enforce storage retention, submit an IRS inventory, approve a use case, complete a PCLIA, or establish an agency system of record.

controls.title: CNG identity evidence names and binds its active backend
controls.scope: CngIdentity stored public/algo/backend metadata and CngLedger signed entry fields
controls.assertion: Run crypto and CNG identity suites.
controls.expected: Stored public-key and backend mismatches fail; signed entries include the active backend; cryptographic vectors and signatures pass.
controls.evidence: pytest output, signed test entries, and the release conformance report
controls.blind_spots: A backend label and algorithm test do not establish FIPS validation, CNSA compliance, hardware protection, or certificate conditions for a deployment.

controls.title: Ultra package excludes local state and test artifacts
controls.scope: The npm artifact produced from ultra_server/package.json
controls.assertion: Run the package-content Node test, which inspects the actual npm pack dry-run manifest.
controls.expected: Only the explicit runtime allowlist plus package.json is present; no logs, restart state, keys, JSON state, or test files are packed.
controls.evidence: Node test output, npm pack manifest, and the release conformance report
controls.blind_spots: This does not make source-relative file dependencies publishable or prove a registry signing/provenance policy.

controls.title: Installed SelfConnect source matches the declared commit pin
controls.scope: The SelfConnect distribution installed in the conformance interpreter and the exact VCS dependency in pyproject.toml
controls.assertion: Read installed direct_url.json and compare its Git commit with the full declared dependency commit.
controls.expected: The installed and declared 40-character commits are identical; the installed package version is reported as metadata, not used as source identity.
controls.evidence: dependency_provenance JSON and the release conformance report
controls.blind_spots: Commit equality does not prove upstream release tagging, package completeness, signature provenance, SBOM attestation, or that a newer commit is compatible.

controls.title: Cross-repository composition uses one verified source lock
controls.scope: SelfConnect SDK dependency identity and the BPC/TSK source checkouts consumed by Enterprise Ultra CI
controls.assertion: Validate portfolio-lock.json, the pyproject SDK pin, CI lock consumption, and any supplied component checkout commits and package metadata.
controls.expected: Every required component has one lowercase 40-character commit; duplicated workflow commits are absent; supplied checkouts exactly match the locked commit, name, and version.
controls.evidence: portfolio_conformance JSON, checkout/build logs, and the release conformance report
controls.blind_spots: Exact source identity does not establish component security, deployment configuration, external storage, key custody, or authorization; a component marked PIN_ONLY requires a composition job to supply its checkout.

controls.title: Production lifecycle operations recover stranded idempotency state
controls.scope: Pair registration, initial TSK provisioning, identity binding, and TSK rotation prepare using PostgreSQL idempotency/resource state
controls.assertion: Run the production live contract with DATABASE_URL, deliberately change each completed idempotency row to processing after its side effect, and retry the signed request.
controls.expected: Each active response is reconstructed under its resource lock, no duplicate pair or TSK resource is created, and ambiguous or inactive durable state fails closed without replacement.
controls.evidence: Live Node output, PostgreSQL resource counts, dependency versions, and deployment commit
controls.blind_spots: The result covers only the four named lifecycle routes and the tested PostgreSQL deployment; new side-effecting routes require their own reconciliation rule and crash-window test.

controls.title: Live Python-to-Node lifecycle contract
controls.scope: A running Ultra Server at the configured endpoint using current Python and Node code
controls.assertion: Start the intended sidecar and run both live contract suites with unavailable-server skipping disabled.
controls.expected: Node live checks and Python tests pass with real HTTP and cryptographic operations.
controls.evidence: Live command output and retained conformance report
controls.blind_spots: Development-mode success does not establish production persistence or restart durability.

controls.title: Production identity and HOTP state survive restart
controls.scope: Production Ultra composition with PostgreSQL, Redis, operator secret, recovery secret, and a killed/restarted Node process
controls.assertion: Run tools.ultra_restart_conformance seed, stop the exact server process, restart it, then run verify against the same state file.
controls.expected: Agent ID, BPC pair, TSK client, HOTP-bearing map, and a post-restart verification remain valid.
controls.evidence: Seed/verify JSON output, service logs, dependency versions, and deployment commit
controls.blind_spots: Cannot be reduced to one safe generic command because process ownership and secret injection are deployment-specific.

controls.title: Shared-state Ultra nodes enforce one fail-closed writer fence
controls.scope: Two production Ultra Node processes on different ports sharing one PostgreSQL database and one Redis fencing authority
controls.assertion: Run the hosted Ultra production durability job's shared-state phase: start both processes fenced, activate one signed epoch, seed a real BPC/TSK principal, promote the other node at a higher epoch, verify the same principal, probe the old and restarted primary, pause Redis, and corrupt the fence record.
controls.expected: Exactly one equal-epoch candidate wins; only the current writer is ready; same-principal verification continues after promotion; the old/restarted primary cannot mutate state; stale, replayed, tampered, unavailable, and corrupt fence conditions fail closed.
controls.evidence: Hosted CI logs and artifacts for Ultra production durability, non-secret service logs, exact portfolio lock, and controlled-drill record
controls.blind_spots: Does not establish independent PostgreSQL/Redis replicas, site/region failover, transactional replication checkpoints, automatic leader election, secret unseal/custody, infrastructure backup restore, RPO/RTO, or authorization. An admitted request may drain under its epoch while its shared PostgreSQL lock prevents a higher epoch's exclusive transition from activating.

controls.title: Production key overlap and retirement ceremony
controls.scope: The selected production Ultra service, its current/previous operator and recovery secrets, PostgreSQL, Redis, and authorized operator clients
controls.assertion: Issue an ephemeral recovery token, rotate to new current plus one previous key, restart and verify overlap, then remove previous keys and verify retirement.
controls.expected: Only the current and immediately previous values work during overlap; after retirement only the new current values work; no secret appears in retained evidence.
controls.evidence: Non-secret status codes, verification booleans, timestamps, service version, dependency versions, and deployment commit
controls.blind_spots: The repository cannot prove an undeployed secret manager, service ACL, personnel custody, or emergency approval process.

controls.title: Ultra disaster recovery is restored, not merely restarted
controls.scope: PostgreSQL, Redis continuity decision, Ultra secrets, agent identity material, signed ledger segments, immutable evidence objects, and the selected deployment boundary
controls.assertion: Restore backups into an isolated environment and execute docs/operations/ULTRA_DISASTER_RECOVERY.md, including restart and immutable-object verification.
controls.expected: Identity, pair, rotated TSK binding, counters, ledger chain, retained provenance, and documented RPO/RTO all verify before service return.
controls.evidence: Restore report, non-secret object identifiers, verification output, recovery point, elapsed time, versions, and commit SHA
controls.blind_spots: A runbook, application restart, or local test database does not prove recoverability of an actual deployment backup.

controls.title: Off-host immutable evidence deployment
controls.scope: Selected provider bucket, retention/legal-hold configuration, credentials, custody, and restore procedure
controls.assertion: Perform provider API retention readback, write/seal/readback, denied overwrite/delete tests, and an isolated restore drill.
controls.expected: Every provider and recovery check passes against the actual deployment boundary.
controls.evidence: Provider API responses without secrets, object/version IDs, receipt hashes, and restore report
controls.blind_spots: Repository tests cannot authorize or inspect an undeployed provider account.

controls.title: Government authorization status
controls.scope: The selected cloud service offering, Mission Owner system, data classification, personnel, and authorization boundary
controls.assertion: Review the authoritative PA/ATO/IATT and RMF package for the exact deployment.
controls.expected: The responsible external authority documents the applicable authorization and conditions.
controls.evidence: Externally issued authorization artifacts and assessor records
controls.blind_spots: No software test can create an ATO, Impact Level authorization, clearance, or classified operating approval.
